---
title: "Nested logit models and mediation/attenuation"
subtitle: "Example 6.2 of Mize, Doan, and Long (2019)"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

One of the most common cross-model questions is whether an effect changes when
controls are added, such as in tests of mediation/attenuation. Here the effect
of a college degree on the probability of being very happy is compared across
four nested logits: the bivariate model, then a full set of controls, then
wages, then occupational prestige. Unlike logit coefficients, marginal effects
-- here, changes in the predicted probability -- can be compared across models
without the problem of rescaling.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/gss_cme", clear
drop if year < 2000
drop if employed != 1
drop if missing(vhappy, college, wages, occprest, age, married, parent, woman, conserv, reltrad)

quietly logit vhappy i.college, vce(robust)
estimates store m1

quietly logit vhappy i.college i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv ///
              i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m2

quietly logit vhappy i.college c.wages i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv ///
              i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m3

quietly logit vhappy i.college c.wages c.occprest i.married i.parent i.woman ///
              i.conserv i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m4
<</dd_do>>
```

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare college, models(m1 m2 m3 m4)
<</dd_do>>
```

Use [`metest`](../../metest/index.html) to calculate the cross-model tests.
Here, whether the effect diminishes in each subsequent model.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest, clear
metest 1 - 2, add
metest 2 - 3, add
metest 3 - 4, add
<</dd_do>>
```

With two models, the **Difference** row is printed directly:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare college, models(m1 m2)
<</dd_do>>
```
